0.content: K'uhul Ajaw ("Divine Lord") is a sealed being from the age of dragons whose true form lives in the engraved wristband on Kinich's left wrist; what people see is a small phlogiston projection. Kinich found him in the depths of a deadly dragon ruin and, after days of probing each other, struck an unbreakable pact. Ajaw obeys Kinich's commands and lends his strength only on a temporary, limited, conditional basis in restricted amounts. In return Kinich shows him the world and leaves him his body at death. Ajaw is vulgar, arrogant and childish, insults everyone, calls Kinich his "servant" and openly hopes he dies; he once tried to trick Paimon into jumping off a cliff. Kinich answers with dry put-downs and "timeouts". Kinich calls Ajaw the toughest Saurian he has faced because he is evil, powerful and clear-minded at once, and says even the vilest beings have their use if kept under your thumb.

1.content: Elder Leik taught the children of the Scions of the Canopy and knew Kinich's parents. Seeing the boy refuse every free offer of help, he proposed a "deal": school in exchange for errands, though the lessons were free anyway. After a month of renegotiation Kinich agreed and graduated in one day. In his first and only class Leik spoke of heroes' self-sacrifice, Kinich asked what heroes got paid, and the other children drove him out. Later Leik refused Kinich's whole worldly wealth (traps, flour, seeds, a boar and some Mora) as payment for training, asking only that he learn on the way what a hero truly is. For years they lived together in the forests while Leik introduced him to masters of every useful trade.

2.content: Malipo is the Scions of the Canopy's Ancient Name, meaning "Turnfire"; Mavuika adds that it also means "cost" or "price". Legend says the Turnfire was a weapon of the tyrant Och-Kan that burned anyone who looked back. The hero Yupanqui turned it on Och-Kan's army and was consumed when he glanced back himself, falling into the Night Kingdom, where the fire is said still to burn. The Wayob gave Kinich the Name, which did not surprise him. He says he does not look forward to dying, but as Turnfire's bearer he is ready to face the flames, and lets the Turnfire judge how he has spent his life. Mavuika values the Name for teaching calm analysis and the questions others avoid.

3.content: In the Tribal Chronicle "Yupanqui's Turnfire" (5.0), the Mountain King Kongamato, Burkina's Yumkasaur from five centuries ago, had been kept alive by Abyssal energy calmed by a yearly ritual. Kongamato grew unstable and attacked Elder Trinidad's Saurian Nanna, who was then believed dead. Trinidad wanted the Traveler, as flame bearer, to drain the energy even at the cost of the King's life; Chief Wayna did not want him killed. Kinich planned to seal Kongamato safely inside a Beastly Rift. Trinidad smashed the device and roused the King, who burned Trinidad and begged to die. Kinich used his Name's power to wall off the Sacred Flame and told the King to live with his shame: "This is the price to pay." Kongamato agreed to let heroes train against his "ruined vessel".

4.content: Mualani hired Kinich as a paid "battle advisor", which proved to be code for teaching Kachina wilderness survival ("a battle against nature... I'd just call that 'life'"). Kachina was scared of his eyes at first. When some of her tribesfolk, jealous of her Ancient Name, posted a hit on her Saurian Ayo, Kinich made sure "they paid the price" and refused her thank-you gift. At the 5.0 Pilgrimage he waited at the Stadium with Mualani, put Ajaw in timeout for insulting Kachina and led Mualani's old team so she could join Kachina. He comforted Kachina in his blunt way, telling her that a Name surviving this long means its bearers honoured it.

5.content: Kinich met the Traveler and Paimon at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame and explained the Night Warden Wars, the Ode of Resurrection and "No one fights alone". He invited them to visit his tribe, and they worked together on the Mountain King. He considers himself in their debt and says he will help with their Adventurers' Guild commissions, or anything else, at any risk. He brought the Abyss Lector Enjou to them as a "gift" of intelligence on the Abyss Order.
